image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Blue 120 litre round plastic waste bin with a domed lid and a rectangular swing flap in the dome, tapered ribbed body, moulded side grip handles, white recycling pictogram panel on the front Materials: sun-bleached blue polyethylene with a chalky matte finish, grey scuffs at the base, faded white pictogram.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93 -- the five layers mean 0.916 and the four critical features 0.930. 1,344/2,000 triangles, 3/3 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 3/4 unique geometries. Everything this round cost was geometry already paid for. What is still simplified: the loops are bar-built with square corners against the plate's rounded D, and band 5 departs from the proxy by 0.120 because the proxy fuses the loops into the body.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.498 x 0.588 x 0.432 m. The body is 10 mm slimmer at every station than it was: the proxy band table read bands 0-3 -- the body's own four -- at a flat +0.017 to +0.021 of H, and a CONSTANT offset across every band is a diameter, not a shape. Those four bands now read -0.013, -0.016, -0.014 and -0.012. The dome (bands 7-8) came in 10 mm as well, from +0.044/+0.045 to +0.021/+0.029.
featureReviews.notes: Band 5 reads -0.120 and is NOT chased. The reference has bands 5 and 6 at the same 0.786 -- a single mass 0.231 m in radius, wider than its own dome -- which is Meshy fusing the two lift handles into the body, exactly the defect the proxy is known for on thin separated members. Dropping the bottom arm and the rail 30 mm to close it was TRIED: it took band 4, where the reference has no lug at all, from +0.015 to +0.136, the worst number the prop has ever carried, and band 5 got worse rather than better.

featureReviews.evidence: The lid now OVERHANGS, which is what a lift-off cap does and what the plate plainly shows: skirt r 0.208-0.214 against a body top of 0.196, an 18 mm overhang. The build had a body top of 0.206 against a skirt of 0.202, so the body's rim poked out past the lid the whole way round. The two lift loops are 30 mm deep, not 62: at 62 they were blocks rather than straps and read as a pair of grey brackets bolted to the bin.
featureReviews.notes: The crown carries a little more radius than the bare ellipse gives it, because the grip lies ACROSS it and on the ellipse the dome had fallen to r 0.085 where the grip is 0.085 wide, putting its two corners through the shell as tabs standing off the silhouette. Flattening the crown far enough to swallow the grip was tried and is worse: at r 0.125 the dome reads as a squashed cap with a hard shoulder and the grip disappears into it. No swing flap: the plate has none, so no flap pivot. The loops are bar-built, so their corners are square where the plate's are rounded.

featureReviews.evidence: Plate crop 204 x 182 px baked to a 256 px WebP on a partial cylinder 3 mm proud following the taper, 0.84 rad, RAISED 40 mm to 0.166-0.286 m. A plate row scan puts the sticker's white between y/H 0.33 and 0.43 and the build's between 0.17 and 0.32 -- a bin whose label sat on its belly rather than its shoulder.

Measured against the plate over three matched bands of the front elevation. Body: plate 93/122/156 luma 117, shipped 92/109/130 luma 106. Lid crown: plate 54/137/196 luma 119, shipped 61/129/178 luma 114. Lid skirt: plate 17/102/162 luma 83, shipped 31/97/147 luma 83.
featureReviews.notes: The body was #99afca and rendered luma 163 against the plate's 110 -- 53 counts too pale, which is most of why the bin read as a pale grey tub under a saturated lid instead of the two-tone bin the plate shows. The harness returns this material close to as authored (174 in, 163 out), so both tones were scaled arithmetically: 0.705 on the body, 0.88 on the lid. Roughness went 0.55 -> 0.72 on BOTH materials at the same time: moulded polyethylene scatters, and at 0.55 the handles' horizontal top faces carried a specular that rendered them as pale grey brackets.

name: Swing-Lid Recycling Bin
nameTh: ถังขยะแยกประเภท
notes: A tapered round polyethylene bin with two side lugs, a domed lift-off lid with a grip slot, and a white recycling sticker on the front. Not breakable; one root pivot, no sockets (the plate shows no swing flap, so no flap pivot). Height corrected from 0.95 to 0.60 at model time from the proxy band table. maxDrawCalls 2 -> 3 and maxMaterials 2 -> 3 (2026-09-01): the plate's body is strongly FLUTED and its dome is SMOOTH, and a canvas tile is per-material, so one material cannot carry both -- fluting the shared material ribbed the dome too, which the reference plainly does not show. The lid (dome, skirt and grip) is therefore its own component on its own material, leaving the body free to carry the stripe tile that is this bin's one real surface feature.
